one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience. I attended for pathology collection and there were around 10 people waiting, but only one staff member appeared to be collecting specimens. There was no clear information about the expected waiting time before I joined the queue.

I was asked to provide a urine sample first, which was fine, but when I asked about my self-collected throat and rectal swabs, I was simply told that I would “do the swabs in the lab”. I explained that one of the specimens was a rectal swab and asked about privacy, but the explanation was unclear and I was not given the swabs at that point.

For a self-collected rectal specimen, clear instructions and an appropriate private space should be explained from the beginning. The communication and organisation were poor, and the whole process unnecessarily wasted my time.

I would strongly recommend that the clinic provide clearer instructions about self-collection, privacy, staffing and expected waiting times before patients are left sitting in a long queue.

We purchased our house-and-land package based on information provided to us about the development, including being told that the project would be completed within approximately one year. It has now been three years, and the project is still not completed.

When we raised our concerns, instead of taking responsibility for the information provided to us, we were told that he was simply passing on what he had been told. For such a major financial investment, we expected much better communication, transparency and accountability.

What is particularly disappointing is that the agent himself purchased land in the same development, and his own house was completed. From our perspective, it was frustrating to see his own project progress while our situation remained unresolved.

This entire experience has caused us considerable stress, inconvenience and disappointment. We expected professionalism, honesty and accountability, and unfortunately that has not been our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Please read before choosing this provider. If I could choose 0 stars, I would!!!!!

I am a single parent living with a brain injury and a significant spinal injury, and I engaged Sensible Health because I genuinely needed support. Unfortunately, my experience has been extremely disappointing and, in my view, deeply distressing.

What started positively gradually changed. I felt that my vulnerability and circumstances were no longer treated with the care, respect and understanding I should have been able to expect from a provider. Instead, I experienced behaviour that I felt was judgmental, intimidating and bullying.

I welcomed support into my home in good faith, only to increasingly feel judged in my own home and made to feel like I was the problem. As someone living with disabilities and raising my Neuro divergent son as a single parent, this had a significant impact on me.

People who seek disability support deserve to feel safe, respected, listened to and genuinely supported  not judged, intimidated, bullied or made to feel that their vulnerabilities are being used for someone else's gain while they judge you instead of supporting aka "their job description"

I have now decided to end my involvement with Sensible Health for good. I shouldn't have to feel guilty, intimidated or made to feel like I am somehow the problem simply because I want to leave and find a more reliable and professional provider.

What has been particularly upsetting is how small and powerless I was made to feel during a time when I was already vulnerable. From my perspective, it felt like my vulnerability was being used for self-gain rather than being treated with the dignity and compassion I deserved.

I am sharing this review because I don't want another vulnerable person or family to experience what I have experienced. Providers working with people with disabilities have an enormous responsibility to treat their clients with dignity, respect, compassion and professionalism.

*Edit* As they now have left me completely let down and stranded without even being sensible or caring or trying to rectify anything I am now happily calling ndis to tell them to Jam the entirety of the stupid NDIS right where the sun don't shine.... Rather be independent with a disability than bwh for people who just drag you down and don't give a damn about anything but themselves and making money 🤑 🤑 🤑 🤑

Sensible Health.....  Thanks for nothing!!! I trusted you with my vulnerability, and in my home and I feel that trust was seriously broken on all standards possible.

I had the great misfortune of being referred to Dr Wright. I took a day off work for a 1:00 pm appointment at Resolve Pain. I arrived on time, but there was no receptionist at the front desk. An elderly couple were already waiting and said they had been there for some time. At 1:10 pm, I called the practice’s landline. Only then did a receptionist come out and direct us to another waiting room.

I waited there until 2:20 pm. The doctor then came out and called a patient who had arrived after me for a 2:00 pm appointment. I explained that my appointment was at 1:00 pm and showed him the confirmation text. After checking his laptop, he said, “Oh well, you’ve been bumped off the list.”

There was no apology, no explanation and no attempt to fit me in. I lost a day’s work, spent well over an hour waiting, and left without the appointment I had booked. For a practice treating people in pain, that lack of care and basic respect was appalling.

Blocked me in my parking spot, waited a good 15-20 mins, walked around asking businesses if the vehicle was a delivery driver for them, no one knew who the truck belonged too. There was no apology for not getting what I asked for but rather I was made to feel guilty for asking for French polish despite offering to come back another day multiple times.

I won’t be coming back here, and I definitely won’t be recommending it to my friends and colleagues who get their nails done.

I am writing to highlight an ongoing issue with TeamMoto Springwood regarding the return of my $500 deposit.

When I put the deposit down, I transferred the money immediately without making them jump through hoops or sign unnecessary forms. However, getting my own money back has been a completely different story.

TeamMoto emailed me their refund form digitally. Since I have no means to print physical documents, I completed and returned it using a verified Adobe Pro digital signature—the exact same software and legal signature format I routinely use to sign major multi-figure contracts. Despite this, TeamMoto Springwood rejected it. To make matters worse, their admin team failed to even notify me of the rejection, leaving the refund stalled until I chased it up myself.

To resolve this simply, I offered to come directly into the store so they could process the refund back onto the original payment card in person, yet this was also refused.

I am asking management to step in, accept the verified paperwork or process the card refund in store, and return my $500 deposit immediately. I will update this review once the matter is resolved.

This has been going on for weeks, just give me my money back! It’s that simple.

Edit: The $500 Deposit was finally returned.
No thanks to their head office, but because I eventually jumped through their administrative hoops, located a printer, and submitted a physical wet-link signature. It shouldn’t take forcing a customer to print physical paperwork in 2026 to return the money that was digitally taken in seconds. My money is back, but the review still stands 1/5.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointed with my experience. I attended for travel advice before a Southern Africa trip and felt I was significantly over-serviced, particularly with the amount of malaria medication I was sold despite questioning whether it was necessary. My GP has since given me quite different advice and also advised he wouldn't have recommended the rabies vaccine for my circumstances as a tourist with no planned animal contact. Overall, the recommendations felt more like a gold-plated approach to travel medicine than advice proportionate to my actual itinerary and risk.

The clinic also attempted to alter the rabies dosing schedule so the doses coincided with when I was able to attend their clinic, even after I explained that I could attend another clinic on the recommended dates. My initial visit cost $870, which was only the first of three rounds of vaccinations. I appreciate that travel medicine involves different assessments of risk, but I left with serious concerns that expensive, highly conservative options were being recommended without adequately distinguishing what was essential from what was optional. I would strongly recommend getting a second opinion before purchasing everything recommended.

I dropped into the shop today fully planning to buy a substantial piece, but I ended up walking out empty-handed because of the customer service.

While I was browsing, I overheard the owner talking to a customer and repeatedly saying "I don't care." Whether that comes down to a language barrier and not having better words to express himself, or just a lack of basic customer care, it’s really off-putting. You just don't use that kind of phrasing with people looking to spend good money in your store.

Buying gold takes a level of trust and clear, respectful communication. The overall vibe felt abrasive, and with so many competing gold shops right on the same street, there’s no reason to settle for a sour experience.

Suggestion for management: Hiring staff or sales representatives who are fluent in English and trained in customer service would go a long way. Better communication would completely transform the shopping environment and keep serious buyers from walking down the street to your competitors.

The estate has the potential to be a beautiful place to live, and being close to the beach is certainly an added bonus. However, based on my experience, I would not choose to purchase with Cedar Woods again.

There were numerous delays with titling. Before purchasing, I raised concerns after seeing social media posts about delays affecting other stages of the development. I was reassured in several emails that the titles for my stage would be delivered within the timeframe advised. Unfortunately, this did not happen, and as a result, my builder substantially increased the cost of my build because the land did not title within the required time-lock period.

The biggest disappointment, however, has been the arrangement with EVE. Buying and building a home is already financially challenging, and in my experience, this arrangement has added significant costs rather than providing the benefit that was presented to residents.

I also feel that Cedar Woods was not sufficiently transparent about what the EVE incentive would mean in practice. It was presented as a positive for residents, but my experience has been the opposite: significantly higher electricity bills, poor customer service, and substantial delays in everything from temporary to permanent power.

What has been particularly frustrating is that residents have raised numerous complaints and concerns, yet I have seen little meaningful action from Cedar Woods to address them.

Overall, while the location and potential of the estate are positives, my experience with Cedar Woods has been extremely disappointing. The delays, additional costs, communication issues and ongoing problems with the EVE arrangement have left me feeling very let down as a homeowner.

I booked a 60 minute skin check appointment for my 26 year old daughter, after researching local providers and reading positive reviews. Her regular doctor was unavailable, so I was hoping to find a thorough alternative.
Unfortunately, the experience was very disappointing. The consultation felt extremely brief, with the skin check completed in just a few minutes. My daughter had questions about several spots on her skin and was interested in discussing the possible removals, but she felt she was quickly brushed off. Rather than receiving detailed explanations or having individual moles carefully examined, she was given a pamphlet and the appointment was effectively over.
The cost was $160, which felt difficult to justify given how brief the consultation was. In the past, she has had skin checks with other doctors who spent considerably more time examining each mole and discussing any concerns in detail.
She left feeling that the appointment was a waste of both time and money. I was particularly disappointed because I had spent considerable time researching the best local option and felt confident based on the reviews. Sadly, our experience did not reflect what we had expected.
If you're looking for a comprehensive and thorough skin check, our experience suggests it may be worth asking in advance how the examination is conducted and how much time is typically spent with patients.

SAFETY & MANAGEMENT CONCERNS
I attended a showcase at Phoenix Studios last week and wanted to provide some constructive feedback, as there is clearly a lot of potential in the venue and the concept.

The venue itself is impressive, with a large open space, high ceilings and an upstairs area. However, I felt the overall experience did not fully match the price of admission, which was approximately $100 for a family of four. The seating consisted of basic plastic-style chairs, and the ticket advertised “nibbles and a drink on arrival.” A modest grazing board and alcoholic drinks were provided.

There were several areas of concern from a safety and event-management perspective.

Most notably, alcohol consumption by some people involved in the event appeared excessive. One of the owners, Paul, appeared visibly intoxicated from the time of our arrival and remained so throughout much of the evening. Given that the event was attended by minors and involved aerial and pole performances, I found this concerning from a professional and safety perspective.

There were also concerns regarding audience management. Some audience members became noticeably intoxicated and disruptive, and the MC was required to intervene and manage their behaviour. There did not appear to be dedicated security or event staff available to manage intoxicated patrons. Given the nature of some of the performances and the presence of dancers, I believe this is an area that warrants serious consideration.

The aerial silks setup also raised concerns for me. The apparatus was positioned at considerable height, and I could not see an obvious safety/rescue system that would allow staff to quickly access a performer in difficulty. Children were also participating on the apparatus. I would strongly encourage management to have the rigging, rescue procedures, supervision and instructor qualifications independently reviewed by an appropriately qualified professional.

The upstairs changing area was another issue. It appeared to be an open stretching area separated from the main space primarily by translucent/see-through curtains and floor mats. This meant that performers changing costumes upstairs could potentially be visible to people in the area below. For a venue hosting predominantly female performers, I believe a genuinely private, secure changing area should be considered.

The use of a professional photographer and designated filming personnel was a positive measure. Unfortunately, the venue layout and positioning of the equipment made it difficult to obtain good footage of some performances. The portable poles also appeared quite dated and moved during some routines, which detracted from the presentation.

The performances themselves were understandably amateur, and I would not expect professional-level choreography from students. However, given the ticket price, I felt the overall production could have been more polished and varied. Some routines appeared to rely heavily on repeated movements, and several performers seemed visibly uncomfortable or under-supported on the night. This is particularly worth addressing given the studio's stated focus on inclusivity, confidence and support.

Finally, I understood that the proceeds from the evening were intended to be donated to the Black Dog Institute. This is a worthwhile cause, and I think attendees would appreciate some follow-up communication confirming the amount raised and/or donated. This is yet to happen.

Overall, I believe Phoenix Studios has significant potential, but I would currently have reservations about attending another showcase or participating as a performer until some of these issues have been addressed. My main concerns are around event safety, alcohol management, performer privacy & safety, aerial rigging and the overall professionalism of event management.

What to expect before you're referred here:
• Contacting this practice by phone or email is close to impossible.
• A referral sent directly from my GP received no response for months.
• If you do get through, expect long hold times, to be spoken to rudely, and to be hung up on mid-conversation.
• I eventually had to withhold my number to get a call answered at all.
• Two reception staff were consistently unprofessional, rude and confrontational — on the phone and in person.

From when you do get through and are able to make a booking, there's a six-month wait to see the specialist, which I can accept — that's become fairly common on the Central Coast and specialist practices are busy. But being unable to reach anyone to even begin the booking process, and being treated with hostility when you finally do get through and attend in person, is a separate problem not excused by patient load or wait times.

Very occasionally I've managed to speak with a receptionist, Kristy, who is polite, professional and helpful — which demonstrates that a reasonable standard is achievable here, and that workload doesn't excuse the contemptuous behaviour from the other reception staff.

He goes up to his tower, everything is fine, he makes lasagna, puts wood in the fire, but then one day he goes to get some wood for the fire, and an unknown guy appears and... A man startles the guard, who says, "Hey, you don't have permission to enter this area." The man replies, "I'm the power repairman." The guard says, "My friend, that generator you're seeing hasn't worked for over three years." Then the man disappears into the forest. He goes to put firewood on the campfire, then a storm hits and the power goes out. Another day passes, and he sees the sunset. He hears the radio; there's smoke. Jack goes to put it out, but it's okay. He puts it out and comes back on. He goes to sleep, and then he hears a cry for help on the radio, but it's not from the other guard. Very disappointed and offended by the time spent talking to Anthony Fillbrook about my matter which is very time-sensitive. I spoke to Anthony for my initial contact where we spent almost one hour discussing my matter; in that time I went over my concerns in detail, some background, as well as shared what I hoped to resolve. Anthony was very generous with his time, shared a lot in terms of the firm's experience in handling matters such as mine, and even suggested a plan where we "could cut costs" which sounded very attractive as my desire was not full-presentation but legal assistance with filling in forms along with some guidance in doing so.

I thought we had a promising and positive interaction, and he even shared such information as where he and his family was heading in the school holidays and that once he visited a long-standing client when she entered an aged facility.

So imagine my confusion when after I had sent him an email with the documents he requested to look over my matter—I never received a reply.

Approximately two weeks after our 58 minute conversation and 8 minute call, I called to gently follow up on my email —Anthony, who picked up the phone, during our 4 minute phone call, claimed "to not remember" me at all. I pointed out the email sent and checked that I had the right email address which he confirmed and then he said he would search for the email and would call me "either way, whether I find it or not."

He never called back. And I called the office two more times leaving a message with reception to which they assured me that Anthony would call back.

Crickets.

Incredibly disrespectful of my time and totally insensitive the fact that I contacted you in good faith for an inquiry where I could potentially become a client.

If you do not have capacity, be upfront. If you have since found that my matter is not one you can assist with, do the right thing and inform me. Pretending that a phone call did not exist and evading contact is not professional.

Phone calls making inquiries are not stand-ins for when you are bored some afternoon at work and want to have a yarn.

Please do better.

Very upsetting experience.

We paid for their youth development program and expected a certified coach to run 2 nights training a week and game days. Instead we were only provided 1 of 2 nights training with a technical staff member and as for the team’s actual coach, I question he even holds any license.
There was an over recruitment of players to the team, which the club didn’t communicate soon enough or manage properly. As a result, players would have to sit out if every player turned up.

The worst of it was the complete lack of professionalism from the coach - no constructive feedback, obvious favoritism shown in game time limits, and singling out players in a humiliating way. The fact that the coach was suspended from match days for 2 weeks at the end of the season speaks volumes. There should be no tolerance for this sort of behaviour at a COMMUNITY level.

We would not recommend this club and its program if you have a child that is seeking quality youth development and to grow their football skills.

I had an extremely disappointing and distressing experience with Times GP Beauty.

I paid $2,000 for two treatment packages and underwent three Picosure treatments. After the second treatment, dark patches suddenly appeared on both sides of my cheeks. Despite this obvious change, I trusted Dr Margaret Chung and proceeded with the third treatment. Unfortunately, my pigmentation became significantly worse afterwards. Given that the pigmentation had already appeared after the second treatment, I question why Dr. Chung proceeded with the third treatment.

The consequences have been both financial and emotional. I have had to use prescription treatment and discard skincare products I purchased from the clinic. I have also become extremely self-conscious about my appearance. I often use my hair to cover my cheeks and avoid looking in the mirror.

I am extremely disappointed with how my concerns have been handled by the clinic management. I paid for treatment expecting improvement, but instead I have been left dealing with a significant pigmentation problem, additional expenses, financial loss and considerable emotional distress.

Based on my personal experience, I strongly do not recommend this clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
READ THE REVIEWS BEFORE YOU GO. We seriously wish we had.

We wanted to support a local business and give it a chance, but instead we wasted money on disappointment and STILL had to stop at KFC on the way home because we were hungry.

The service was terrible from the moment we walked in. The staff saw us enter and couldn’t even be bothered acknowledging us. One guy was sitting there on the phone having what sounded like a personal conversation with his girlfriend. We stood there wondering how we were even supposed to order until he eventually pointed at the ipad, basically telling us to order ourselves.

Then came the food.

The photos displayed on the banner are completely misleading compared with what you actually receive. We expected a decent portion that could feed two people. Instead, the portions were ridiculously small, literally around FIVE tiny pieces of chicken per combo.

And before anyone says “you get what you pay for”: $50 for a combo box should at least buy you enough food for a meal.

If the chicken had been exceptional, full of flavour and genuinely high quality, maybe the price and tiny portions could be justified. But it wasn’t. It was bland, dry and had the texture of cardboard. There was nothing “premium” about it.

We left hungry and had to BUY MORE FOOD ON THE WAY HOME.

And let’s be realistic, chicken is not some luxury ingredient. Few tiny pieces for what we paid is completely ridiculous.

Honestly, this felt like an absolute waste of money. The portion sizes, food quality, service and misleading presentation were all disappointing.

And after reading through the reviews, I’m genuinely questioning how this place has such a high rating. Some of the good reviews look suspiciously similar and overwhelmingly positive compared with the experience we had.

DO YOURSELF A FAVOUR: READ THE REVIEWS, LOOK AT THE ACTUAL CUSTOMER PHOTOS AND THINK TWICE BEFORE SPENDING YOUR MONEY HERE.

We came in wanting to support a local business. Instead, we left feeling completely ripped off.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆

THE WORST PSYCHOLOGY SERVICE. More cancellations than actual sessions.

MeHelp Psychology has been an absolutely appalling experience. This was my FIRST EVER experience seeking therapy, and honestly, I could not have imagined a worse introduction to psychological support.

I have experienced MORE cancellations than actual sessions. Let that sink in. I made the decision to seek professional help, took the time to arrange appointments, prepared myself for sessions and even took time off work, only to be repeatedly let down by cancellations.

The latest incident was the final straw. My appointment was confirmed just the day before, only for me to receive a cancellation message a few hours before the scheduled session. No consideration for my time, my preparation or the effort it takes to make these appointments happen.

Seeking therapy in the first place can be difficult enough. You are making yourself vulnerable and taking steps to look after your wellbeing. To then be met with repeated cancellations, unreliability and what has felt like a complete lack of professionalism is incredibly disheartening.

I came here looking for help, not to have an already difficult period of my life made more stressful by the very service I turned to for support. This experience has caused me additional distress rather than providing the consistent support I was hoping for.

The reliability and professionalism I expected from a psychology service have been seriously lacking in my experience. I am genuinely appalled that this has been my introduction to therapy.

Management needs to take a serious look at how this service is being run. People seeking psychological support deserve reliability, consideration and basic professionalism, not repeated last-minute cancellations and wasted time.

I would NOT recommend MeHelp Psychology to my worst enemy. If this is how they treat people trying to access support, they need to do considerably better or just close the place down entirely. Absolutely unacceptable.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience with Yellow Bridge has been extremely disappointing, particularly in relation to communication, transparency, support coordination and the handling of concerns about my services.

As an NDIS participant, I expect my support coordinator and the organisation they work for to act professionally, communicate openly and ensure that decisions affecting my supports are handled appropriately. Unfortunately, my experience has left me with serious concerns about whether these expectations have been met.

One of my main concerns relates to communication and transparency regarding contact with other providers involved in my supports. I believe participants should be kept appropriately informed about communication and decisions that may affect their services. When this transparency is lacking, it undermines trust and makes it difficult for participants to feel confident that their interests and preferences are being properly considered.

I am also concerned about the impact that decisions and communication surrounding my supports have had on services that are important to my goals and wellbeing. Support coordination should help participants navigate the NDIS, work collaboratively with providers, resolve issues and maintain appropriate support arrangements wherever possible. It should not leave participants feeling excluded from decisions, uncertain about what is happening or forced to repeatedly advocate for themselves to have their concerns acknowledged.

What has made this experience particularly frustrating is the loss of trust that has developed. A support coordination relationship requires clear communication, accountability and a willingness to listen when a participant raises legitimate concerns. When those expectations are not met, it can become extremely difficult to maintain a productive working relationship.

I have reached the point of formally requesting a change in support coordination because I no longer have confidence in the current arrangement. I believe participants should be able to raise concerns about their services and request changes without feeling that their concerns are being overlooked.

I also believe management has a responsibility to take complaints seriously, investigate concerns fairly and ensure that participants receive appropriate communication about matters affecting their supports.

I would like Yellow Bridge to reflect on how it handles communication with participants, transparency when liaising with other providers, complaints and requests for changes to support coordination.

NDIS participants deserve to feel heard, respected and involved in decisions affecting their lives. They should not have to lose confidence in their support coordination before their concerns receive meaningful attention.

Based on my experience, I would encourage prospective clients to ask detailed questions about communication practices, participant involvement in decision-making, complaint handling and the process for changing support coordinators before engaging with this organisation.

As a same sex couple wanting to start our fertility journey, we made our first enquiry with rainbow fertility.
Unfortunately, we were incredibly disappointed with our experience.

As a plus size couple we knew our BMIs could be an issue with certain fertility clinics & ensured to ask if this would be an issue when we first spoke with Rainbow Fertility. We were assured that Rainbow Fertility takes a wholistic approach and looks at a range of factors but clearly the fertility Dr we were referred to by Rainbow Fertility (Dr Georgiana Tang) did not get the memo.

Without reviewing any of the results we’d sent from the testing we’d had done, Dr Tang said that she would not even consider doing IVF until I had lost at least 30kgs and ideally 40 based purely on my BMI.

We found Dr Tang rude and unprofessional in a number of other ways such as not providing the correct information about the appointment location, stating that she had not received our testing results and refusing to review them until we asked multiple times and told her we were told they’re in the database multiple times and giving us information that is in contradiction to information given by other specialists.

On top of this, for a company that promotes themselves as LGBTIQ specialists, the language used during the consult was wildly heteronormative.

After this experience, we decided to try a different fertility clinic and the experience has been so much better. The testing suggested by the rainbow fertility GP was also pretty basic and basically a waste of time and money as we needed to complete more comprehensive testing when we started with the new clinic.

The process of accessing fertility treatment can be long and expensive. I wouldn’t waste time or money going through rainbow fertility.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and appalled by my experience with Mindstate Consulting and the way my ADHD assessment and treatment pathway has been handled.

I specifically chose Mindstate Consulting over other providers because I was told they could offer a much faster pathway to diagnosis and medication due to their partnership with psychiatrist Dr Hudson Aly. Timing was extremely important to me because I was about to start a new job and wanted to have my diagnosis and treatment underway as soon as possible.

I was upfront about this from the beginning. I was told that getting medication before starting my new job would be difficult, but that it was possible within the first 2–3 weeks of starting.

It has now been FOUR MONTHS since I started my new job, and I still have not even had an appointment with Dr Hudson Aly.

Had I been told from the beginning that I could potentially be waiting four months or longer just for the psychiatrist appointment, I would have seriously reconsidered choosing Mindstate Consulting. The faster pathway they presented was a major factor in my decision to proceed with them.

What makes this considerably worse is the complete lack of proactive communication throughout the process. I have had to follow up multiple times myself simply to find out what is happening. There have been periods of radio silence where I have received no meaningful updates unless I actively chased them.

I find this level of communication and organisation completely unacceptable for a service dealing with people’s mental health. This is particularly disappointing given that Nick, the owner of Mindstate Consulting, is responsible for overseeing the service and ensuring that patients receive clear communication and appropriate support throughout their care pathway.

I understand that psychiatrist availability and delays can be outside a provider’s control, and I understand that medication itself can never be guaranteed. What I cannot accept is setting an expectation of weeks and allowing that timeframe to stretch into months without proper communication, transparency or accountability.

If the expected timeframe changes, patients should be proactively informed. They shouldn’t be left wondering what is happening and repeatedly forced to chase the service themselves..

The experience has been extraordinarily frustrating and, in my opinion, extremely unprofessional. I expected far better processes, communication and accountability from a mental health service.

If you’re considering Mindstate Consulting specifically because you’re expecting a fast pathway to psychiatric care, I strongly recommend getting their current expected psychiatrist waiting time in writing before proceeding.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Mindstate Consulting.

I had a beard transplant 11 months ago, but unfortunately, I’m very unhappy with the result. The clinic and surgeon told me that 1,500 grafts were transplanted.

I tried contacting both the surgeon and the clinic several times to discuss my concerns, but unfortunately, I haven’t received a response or been contacted by the surgeon.

Because I couldn’t get a response from the original surgeon, I consulted other hair-transplant surgeons for their opinions. One surgeon examined my beard and estimated that I may have received only around 200 grafts. Another surgeon estimated that the number could be around 400 grafts.

This is obviously very concerning to me, especially because I was told that 1,500 grafts had been transplanted.

Now i have to get the surgery redone by another surgeon and i wasted 11 months waiting for that claimed beard to grow.

I attached 2 photos for the same day of the surgery.
